subject: SDLC evidence: deployment bisection, signed artifacts, and ephemeral KMS handover
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria@auditcorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDLC evidence ask — artifact signing + canary validation

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this. For our SOC2 scope we need a compact package showing how you: 1) sign build artifacts in CI, 2) validate canary releases and gate promoted images, and 3) hand off short-lived KMS/HSM keys during rollout/rollback.

Can you provide:
- a single-page checklist that your engineers use to validate a canary (metrics and thresholds),
- the CI job names and a sample command showing how an artifact is signed and the signing key id,
- a short chronological timeline of key rotations for ephemeral signing keys used in the last 90 days, and
- a copy of your rollback playbook (high level).

If any of this is sensitive, redacted artifacts are fine — but include the exact commands and job names so we can map to pipeline logs.

Targeting a quick review on Friday; let me know if you need more time.

Best,
Maria
AuditCorp
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria@auditcorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence ask — artifact signing + canary validation

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial bundle: canary-validation-checklist.pdf, artifact-signing-keys.csv (redacted key ids), and rollback-playbook.md.

Quick notes:
- CI job names: pipeline_build, pipeline_sign, pipeline_promote. See attached CSV for key aliases and rotation windows (redacted last 4 chars).
- Signing command (example): 
  gpg --output artifact.sig --detach-sign --local-user REDWOOD_SIGNER_01 build/output/my-service-20270629.tar.gz
  The CI job pipeline_sign runs on a detached HSM-backed signing agent; we store aliases in Vault and only export ephemeral signing tokens to the agent for the job duration.
- Canary validation: checklist includes CPU/latency P50/P95 thresholds, error-rate delta, and a traffic-slice rollback threshold.
- Rollback playbook: includes bisection steps (reduce slice, redeploy previous signed artifact, revoke ephemeral token), incident roles (oncall, release owner) and postmortem hooks.

We still need to extract a concise rotation timeline for your request; Jordan will push a CSV shortly. If you want raw pipeline logs, we can provide a redacted excerpt.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Head of Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: canary-validation-checklist.pdf (pdf), artifact-signing-keys.csv (csv, redacted), rollback-playbook.md (markdown)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria@auditcorp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence ask — artifact signing + canary validation

Maria / team — adding the technical bits you can map to logs: 

1) CI jobs and example snippets (pipeline names are exact):
- pipeline_build (step: build:docker-build) produces image tag: registry.redwood/infra/my-service:${BUILD_NUMBER}
- pipeline_sign (step: sign:artifact-sign) runs on pool: signing-agents-hsm; job calls the internal tool signctl:
  signctl sign --artifact registry.redwood/infra/my-service:${BUILD_NUMBER} --key-alias ephemeral-signer-2027-06 --out artifact.sig
- pipeline_promote (step: release:canary-promote) applies k8s manifest with image digest pinned to the signed artifact.

2) Ephemeral key flow (high level):
- Key material stored in HSM (thales-hsm-1).
- On pipeline initiation, Vault issues a short-lived wrapping token to the signing agent via AppRole; token TTL = 15m.
- signctl requests HSM to sign using key alias; HSM only returns signature blob, not private key.

3) Rotation timeline (preview):
- ephemeral-signer-2027-04 rotated 2027-04-12 (reason: scheduled rotation)
- ephemeral-signer-2027-05 rotated 2027-05-09 (reason: scheduled rotation)
- ephemeral-signer-2027-06 rotated 2027-06-22 (reason: scheduled rotation)
Full CSV with UTC timestamps attached as rotation-timeline.csv.

4) Canary validation metrics mapping (what we log):
- metric keys: service.latency.p50, service.latency.p95, service.errors.rate_5m, service.cpu.
- Canary policy: if errors.rate_5m increases > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency delta > 40% => auto-reduce traffic slice to 5% and notify oncall.

If you need a redacted pipeline log line for an explicit build number, tell us the build number and we will extract the snippet.

-Jordan
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maria Torres <maria@auditcorp.com>

Thanks Jordan — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications:
1) Can you confirm whether the signing agent ever has persistent access to private key material (yes/no)?
2) Please include the CSV column headers you used for rotation-timeline.csv (we need to map fields).

If you can drop those two items and a redacted log line for build number 4238 we can close the quick pass.

Cheers,
Maria
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria@auditcorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, DevOps Lead <ops@veridianbank.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence ask — deployment bisection package and rotation timeline

Maria — final bundle below. Responses inline and a short excerpt of the pipeline log attached.

Responses:
- Does signing agent ever have persistent key material? No. The signing agent receives a Vault-wrapped ephemeral token; private key material remains in the HSM and is never exported. We have an internal design doc that states this as an invariant.
- rotation-timeline.csv headers: key_alias, rotation_iso_utc, rotated_by, rotation_reason, previous_key_alias, note

Attached: rotation-timeline.csv (full UTC timestamps), canary-run-excerpt.log (redacted), rollback-playbook.md (finalized with bisection step), plus the previous attachments.

We also uploaded the package to secure drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/SDLC-AUDIT-2027 (shared read-only link, auditor group).

If you want the redacted pipeline log for build 4238 specifically, Jordan has placed the single-line snippet in canary-run-excerpt.log (line shows signctl call and resulting artifact digest). Otherwise, please confirm receipt and we'll mark the ticket (JIRA INF-4127) as evidence-delivered.

Best regards,
Evelyn
Head of Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference
